35.63062,-80.8636: Blue Star Memorial Highway A tribute to the Armed Forces that have defended the United States of America sponsored by Statesville Garden Council in cooperation with The Garden Club of North Carolina, Inc. and North Carolina Department of Transportation
35.65368,-80.58595: Francis Locke 1722 1796. Colonel of Whig force which routed Tories at Battle of Ramsour's Mill, June 20, 1780. Home stood nearby.
35.72282,-80.89669: Barium Springs Home For Children. Formerly Presbyterian Orphans Home. Opened here in 1891 by Synod of N.C. Jethro Rumple was first chair, Board of Regents.
35.78135,-80.89185: Mitchell College. Founded 1856 as college for women. Presbyterian until 1959. Granted state community college status, 1973. Two blocks N.
35.78138,-80.89174: Vance House. Now historical museum, was temporary home of Gov. Zebulon B. Vance after Sherman's capture of Raleigh, April 1865. Is 350 yards southwest.
35.7815,-80.89162: J. P. Caldwell. Editor of Statesville "Landmark" (1880-92), Charlotte "Observer" (1892-1909). His home was two blocks north.
35.78394,-80.88533: Stoneman's Raid. On a raid through western North Carolina Gen. Stoneman's U.S. cavalry occupied Statesville, April 13, 1865.
35.78533,-80.89093: Fourth Creek Meeting House. Presbyterian. Established ca. 1750; on this site by 1756. The Rev. James Hall first regular minister.
35.82601,-80.87506: Fort Dobbs. Built in 1756 by colony. Was garrisoned by North Carolina Provincials during French & Indian War, until 1762. Site 1 mi. N.
35.89318,-80.95069: Clio's Nursery. A school established about 1778 by the Rev. James Hall. Trained many prominent men. Closed about 1787. Was a few hundred yards E.
35.912,-80.95242: William Sharpe 1742 1818. Member of Continental & provincial congresses; was first legislator to advocate U.N.C., 1784. Grave is 2 miles east.
